parts: Please see /papers/investigations-3/brainstorm/notes/02_FIXED_CHARACTER_GOALS_AND_ARITHMETIC_COLLISION_RESEARCH_CODEX_20261018.md. Let's brainstorm a list of new projects to add to investigations-3 based on these new considerations.
I’ll read the note and the repository’s research guidance, then develop a shortlist of new investigations with concrete questions and first tests.

The note shifts the priority toward arithmetic constraints that survive heat flow and affect a fixed function’s collisions. I’m checking the existing projects and corrected control arguments so the shortlist targets missing estimates rather than repackaging known criteria. I’ll use the writing skill to save the brainstorm in the repository’s established notes format.

A useful opening is that the repository already has exact arithmetic identities, but the attempted estimates often lose the cancellation those identities preserve. I’m separating projects that could control those complete expressions from projects that test whether local collisions force a detectable violation of the global arithmetic constraints.

One distinct candidate is the fixed Dirichlet beta function, whose theta kernel has an exact Dedekind-eta product. That gives a concrete way to pursue your “at least one fixed character” objective. I’m including it alongside the zeta projects, while keeping family-to-fixed-function transfer as a separate question that needs an actual transfer theorem.

I’ve narrowed the shortlist to five projects, each with a first substantive result and a control test. The strongest starting combination looks like coupled arithmetic dilations, modular auxiliary functions, and the fixed beta-function project. The oscillator and collision-scale approaches remain worthwhile higher-risk options with specific gaps to resolve.

I’d propose **five projects**, keeping the existing collision criterion fixed and directing the new work toward arithmetic estimates. My preferred starting set is **09, 10, and 12**.

| Proposed project | Central idea | First meaningful result |
|---|---|---|
| **08 — Modular oscillator estimates** | Combine the theta-jet recurrence with full modular reflection to constrain the signed physical observation. This gives geometric and octonionic methods a specific estimating task. | A valid trace or bilinear inequality that uses both arithmetic constraints and retains all boundary costs. |
| **09 — Coupled arithmetic dilation estimates** | Estimate the complex-shifted theta field together with its lower-interval correction, preserving the cancellation in the exact arithmetic packets. | A signed packet estimate with controlled dependence on time, strip width, and cutoff. This is the most direct continuation of 21–22. |
| **10 — Modular auxiliary functions** | Construct modular test functions that yield a lower bound for the existing collision form. | One useful auxiliary functional with a proved sign and complete tail control. This is the boldest construction project. |
| **11 — Arithmetic constraints at collision scale** | Match the universal local collision profile to global modular or dilation relations, and identify information that survives this matching. | A quantitative arithmetic restriction on a possible collision, or a precisely scoped obstruction showing which measurements lose that information. |
| **12 — Fixed Dirichlet beta function** | Study \(L(s,\chi_{-4})\) using its exact Dedekind-eta product kernel, holding the character fixed throughout. | A signed heat-transform estimate that exploits the complete product and modular relations. This directly serves your fixed-character objective. |

**09 has the clearest immediate connection to the missing step.** The exact formulas and their failed separations are already known. The research question is whether estimating the complete expression reveals a usable arithmetic constraint.

**10 brings in a substantially different construction method.** Modular Fourier interpolation provides a concrete source of techniques, although adapting its sampling and function-space requirements to the collision observable is itself a serious problem. [Radchenko–Viazovska](https://arxiv.org/html/1701.00265)

**12 is especially worth considering.** The beta function has the positive, even source
\[
\Psi_\beta(u)=e^{3u}\eta(ie^{4u})^3.
\]
Its exact product supplies a specific arithmetic structure to investigate. Product positivity alone does not determine the Fourier sign, but this gives us a concrete fixed function with a different analytic starting point. [Jacobi product](https://dlmf.nist.gov/20.4.E2), [eta identity](https://dlmf.nist.gov/23.15.E9)

I would treat **08 as a principal alternative if we want the geometric emphasis**, and **11 as the most exploratory option**. Progress should mean a new arithmetic restriction, an applicable transfer theorem, or a useful scoped obstruction; an immediate numerical improvement need not be the deciding test.

I saved the [full brainstorm note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/brainstorm/notes/03_NEW_FIXED_FUNCTION_PROJECTS_CODEX_20261018.md), including proposed folder names, control screening, specialist audiences, and the beta normalization. I understand it is the most exploratory, but maybe we can make it more precise, but before we do that I want to make sure we have all of the proposals outlined more

I’ll create homes for all five projects and a shared exploratory research overview, with a fuller proposal in each project. I’ll mark 11 as your preferred next direction and sharpen its opening questions while keeping the immediate work focused on outlining the full set.

I’m separating what each project can take as established from the new result it would need to produce. For 11, the opening question will be more concrete: can an exact global arithmetic relation impose a restriction that the universal local collision model cannot see?

The outlines now give each project a first research task, a control check, and a clear account of what would count as progress. For 11, I’ve narrowed the starting point to a double collision and the complete \(d=2\) dilation relation, with full modular compatibility as a second route.

Project 11’s outline now separates the local collision expansion from the shifted arithmetic terms that remain outside it. I’m also making each proposal stand on its own, with links to the existing evidence and a clear distinction between established formulas and conjectured advances.

The five proposals and shared overview are drafted. I’m checking their cross-references and folder structure, including the distinction between 09’s packet estimates and 11’s collision-scale question, before saving them into the repository.
The folder structure and local links check out. I’m saving the five project homes now, each with an expanded proposal, and updating the portfolio index to mark 11 as your preferred next direction.
